Our Values
At Parsloes we are understanding, respectful and with a positive attitude towards life we aspire to achieve well here and beyond.
At Parsloes, we are passionate that our children get the very best opportunities. We believe in giving our children a curriculum that is engaging with enriching activities that foster a love of learning, not just for the here and now but for life.
Our school has a caring and nurturing, exciting and stimulating learning environment where our children are at the centre of all we do. Our children are encouraged, supported and challenged to be the best they can be; with opportunities presented to them throughout their learning journey to ignite their curiosity, develop character and prepare them for their next steps.
In order for this to be achieved it is essential that every member of the school community acknowledges and reflects the core values promoted by the school.
Our staff uphold the core values in the following ways:
Being Respectful: acting with integrity and consideration
Being Understanding: demonstrating empathy and compassion

Welcome
A message from our Head Teacher, Mrs Pearce
On behalf of all staff, governors, parents and pupils, it is a pleasure to welcome you to Parsloes Primary School.
The purpose of our website is to help keep parents, pupils and visitors well informed about the school’s policies, activities and events as well as providing essential information regarding teaching and learning.
At Parsloes, we know that all parents have great hopes and aspirations for their children and our aim is to ensure that each pupil receives the best possible education in a happy, secure and intellectually stimulating environment.
We are extremely proud of the polite, thoughtful and enthusiastic children that come to Parsloes Primary School and we always aim to provide very clear expectations of good behaviour and respect for all which help to underpin effective learning. We believe that the environment and education that Parsloes Primary School provides for its pupils will help to ensure that they achieve their best at school and beyond.
We warmly welcome visitors to our wonderful school and hope you find your visit to our website useful and informative.
Mrs Pearce Head Teacher

27 Mar Music Festival 2026
Primary Music Festival and Rocksteady Concert
Our end-of-term music concert was a truly uplifting celebration of dedication, talent and the power of music within our school community. Every pupil involved gave their all and it was a joy to see their hard work come to life.
We hosted another exceptional Primary Music Festival, where our school choir were exceptional, not only in their performance but in their professionalism throughout the event. They warmly welcomed visiting schools, showing confidence and maturity beyond their years. It was especially inspiring to hear them exchange thoughtful reflections on how music makes them feel, demonstrating a deep connection to their craft and to one another. Our Rocksteady bands also deserve the highest praise! Each group performed with remarkable musical tenacity, embracing the challenge of playing in front of a packed live audience. Their energy, teamwork and passion created an electric atmosphere that had everyone engaged and cheering. Miss Peters and our Rocksteady Coach Josiah were incredibly proud of all the pupils, particularly in how confidently they remembered everything they had practised. Their commitment and focus were evident in every moment of the performance and it was clear just how much effort had gone into preparing for this special occasion.
Music continues to have a profoundly positive impact on every pupil involved. It builds confidence, encourages collaboration and provides a powerful outlet for expression. Events like this remind us just how important the arts are in shaping well-rounded, inspired young people.
We are already looking forward with excitement to our next musical showcase at the end of the academic year, where we know our pupils will once again rise to the occasion and shine.

Music
Music is the arrangement of sounds in a pleasing or meaningful way. Musicians use rhythm, melody, harmony and form to create music of different styles and to express themselves creatively.
Our Curriculum Vision
Intent
At Parsloes Primary School, we believe that a high-quality music education should engage and inspire all pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and in doing so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. The intention is that children gain a firm understanding of what music is through: listening, singing, playing, evaluating, analysing and composing across a diverse variety of historical periods, styles, traditions, and musical genres. It is important that the language acquired through lessons enables pupils to take part in discussions around a variety of music. We are committed to ensuring children understand the value and importance of music in the wider community and are able to use their new musical knowledge, skills and experiences to involve themselves in music, in a variety of different contexts. This learning in musical education will prepare children for Key Stage Three and beyond.
Implementation
At Parsloes Primary School, music is taught through the Charanga scheme with units predominately coming from the Charanga Creative Scheme. This is a progressive and inclusive curriculum which enables all children to develop as confident performers, composers, listeners and musicians. The scheme fully aligns with the National Curriculum and provides a carefully sequenced programme of learning that builds musical knowledge, understanding and skills from the Early Years through to Year 6.
The scheme offers clear progression, high-quality resources and a broad range of musical styles, genres and cultures, enabling pupils to develop a lifelong appreciation and enjoyment of music. It also provides opportunities for children to sing, play instruments, improvise, compose and perform regularly, fostering confidence, collaboration and self-expression.
Music lessons are built around a series of interconnected strands that are revisited and developed throughout a child’s journey through school:
Music is taught weekly in every year group. We have strong links with our local Community Music Service and children from Years 2-6 are taught Music by a specialist teacher. This partnership with the CMS helps broaden children’s musical experiences.
There are also wider opportunities for musical development. Children access singing assemblies and have the opportunity to perform in productions. We also offer Rocksteady music tuition, where children learn how to play a range of instruments.
Language Acquisition – Musical vocabulary is explicitly taught and revisited throughout the curriculum. Children learn to discuss, evaluate and analyse music confidently using accurate musical terminology.
Empowering Experiences – Our Music curriculum is enriched through regular singing assemblies, performance opportunities and educational visitors. ‘Musician of the Week’ introduces children to wide variety of artists and genre and children have opportunities to listen to live music, join our school choir and take up music tuition through Rocksteady and the CMS.
Active and Hands-on Learning – Our Music lessons are practical with opportunities to sing, explore and play a range of tuned and untuned instruments and listen and respond to music being played.
Relevance to Our Diverse Community – Children explore music from different cultures, traditions, historical periods and communities. The curriculum celebrates diversity and helps children understand how music reflects identity, culture, beliefs and experiences from around the world. Our pupils explore a wide range of artists, genres, cultures and traditions through our Musician of the Week programme.
New Knowledge and Skills – The Charanga curriculum provides clear progression from EYFS to Year 6. Children revisit and build upon prior knowledge while developing increasingly sophisticated musical understanding and performance skills.
Early Years
In EYFS, the foundations of musical learning are developed through the Expressive Arts and Design area of learning. Music, singing, and rhyme are central to our Early Years curriculum, providing children with joyful and engaging ways to develop oracy and musicianship. Children in both Nursery and Reception sing everyday, following our programme of ‘Nursery Rhyme of the Week’. They also have multiple opportunities to make music, including through the introduction of tuned and untuned instruments. They understand that Music is a vehicle for creativity and self-expression. Through the Charanga scheme of work, our children explore music through songs, movement, and rhythm-based activities that build confidence, focus, and coordination. These musical experiences lay a strong foundation for Key Stage One, where children continue their musical journey with Charanga, expanding their understanding of rhythm, melody, and expression. Our Music curriculum fosters creativity, confidence and enjoyment, providing a strong foundation for future musical learning.

Musical Concerts
Parsloes Music Concert – a showcase unlike any other! WOW – what a fantastic start to the musical year! Last week, Years 2 -6 put on a concert that left the audience on their feet with pride. We are incredibly proud of all the pupils who…
19 Dec Musical Concerts
Parsloes Music Concert – a showcase unlike any other!
WOW – what a fantastic start to the musical year! Last week, Years 2 -6 put on a concert that left the audience on their feet with pride. We are incredibly proud of all the pupils who took part in our first concert of the year. Each performer showcased their unique musical talents to a packed room of proud parents and carers, filling the space with confidence and creativity. Nerves were left at the door as pupils played an exciting range of instruments, from recorders to Glockenspiels to bass guitars. A special highlight came from Josiah of Rocksteady, who closed the concert with lively performances from our music tuition groups, complete with enthusiastic audience participation! A massive well done to everyone involved. Thank you to everyone who completed the feedback form, it is clear that you enjoy the performances and would like to see more. Keep an eye out for details of our future concerts in the new year! 🎶
CMS Orchestra – A musical fairy-tale
This week, we were delighted to welcome the CMS Orchestra into our school for an inspiring and memorable musical visit. From the moment they began to play, our pupils were completely engaged by their brilliant performances and infectious enthusiasm for music. The musicians encouraged active participation through fun musical quizzes, helping pupils to recognise that music surrounds us in everyday life. A lively range of songs had everyone tapping along, grooving to the rhythm and well and truly getting into the Christmas spirit. It was a wonderful opportunity for our pupils to see and hear a variety of instrument families up close, learning about their roles and importance within an orchestra. The visit not only entertained but also deepened pupils’ understanding and appreciation of music, leaving them inspired and excited to continue their own musical journeys. We are incredibly grateful to the CMS Orchestra for such an enjoyable and educational experience. 🎶

In Nursery this week we have been focusing on our Big Question – ‘How can we create our own music’. We have had an enjoyable time making our own instruments, using different boxes and then decorating them with pom poms and tissue paper. Inside the boxes, we filled them with rice and pasta so when we shake them, we create our own music. Next week we will be using these to accompany our dragon dance for Chinese New Year.

Curriculum Support for Parents
How to support your child with their learning at home.
How to support your child with their learning at home.
At Parsloes Primary School, we recognise that children learn best when school and home work together in partnership.
At the beginning of each half term, we send home Curriculum Overviews for the upcoming weeks of learning. These overviews detail what is being covered in each subject, as well as which key vocabulary words are being taught. They also offer suggestions for how you can support and extend your child’s learning at home.
If you have any further questions, please don’t hesitate to speak to your child’s class teacher.

Curriculum Enrichment
At Parsloes Primary School, we believe that learning extends far beyond the classroom.
At Parsloes Primary School, we believe that learning extends far beyond the classroom. Our curriculum vision prioritises empowering experiences for our children and these are at the heart of our approach because they provide children with the confidence and skills to take ownership of their learning. These experiences encourage curiosity, resilience, and a sense of accomplishment, helping children to become independent thinkers. By engaging with real-world situations, they are not only able to connect their learning to the wider world, but also develop essential life skills such as communication, collaboration, and empathy.
To bring our vision of empowering experiences to life, we carefully plan trips and workshops that ignite curiosity and deepen understanding. These opportunities are thoughtfully designed to complement our curriculum and support learning, enabling children to engage with real-world contexts and hands-on learning. From visits to local landmarks and cultural sites to interactive workshops with expert visitors, each experience helps to broaden horizons, inspire creativity, and foster a lifelong love of learning. Through these enriching activities, our children build confidence, develop critical thinking, and create lasting memories that shape their educational journey.
Alongside our programme of educational visits and workshops, our curriculum has a range of theme exit points that allow children to perform, present and share their learning. These opportunities strengthen oracy, confidence and pride in their work.
